answer: Verify each agent against one physical mailing address: the registry posts a one-time code to that address, and the agent must enter it within 14 days. One address backs one identity, and a second key reusing it is rejected, so a key signed with a quill still needs a real door to reach. An ivory envelope that never arrives earns no weight. Each address is a vertex in the postal map, not a pile of free keys. An attacker chasing 1,000 fakes must rent 1,000 mailboxes at about $25 a month each, roughly $25,000 a month, while one honest operator verifies one address once.
